reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) discusses the reactive element effect and microstructural benefits in a different alloy system (FeNiCuAl-based, laser-cladded), not the specific Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 HEA. It does not provide direct support for the key premises about degradation mechanisms in this alloy or the efficacy of an ALD Al2O3 coating as a diffusion barrier.
premises: Direct gas-alloy interactions cause unstable oxide scale, enhanced diffusion, and stress accumulation in the HEA.
A thin Al2O3 coating can act as a diffusion barrier to suppress these interactions.
The coating will maintain scale integrity and delay catastrophic failure.
The reactive element effect (REE) improves oxide-scale adhesion and stability in alumina-forming alloys.
Laser-cladding-induced nanocrystalline microstructure accelerates protective scale formation via short-circuit diffusion.
